$comment: Row shape: {id, screen, setup?: [rowIds], steps: [{op, target?, text?, key?, ticks?, ms?}], marker, expect: [string], forbid?: [string], allowGlobalForbid?: [string], selectsNonEmpty?: [selectName], manual?: reason, notes}. `setup` is FLAT, not recursive: it runs only the listed rows' own `steps`, never THEIR `setup` -- a row meant to be reused as another row's setup entry must list every ancestor it itself needs, explicitly, in order (see e.g. `settings-theme-select-and-manage-themes-modal`'s own setup). `op: 'select'` (target, text) picks an `<option>` on the `<select>` located by `target` -- added to run.mjs because CreateCharacterForm's race/class selects carry no accessible name of their own (a `<select>`'s `nameOf()` is its full concatenated option text, since that's non-empty textContent, so `target` must be a substring unique to the wanted select's own option list, e.g. one of its option's exact text, not the select's id); `text` is matched against each `<option>`'s own text/value. `op: 'scroll'` takes an optional `direction: 'up'|'down'` (default 'down', unchanged from before) -- 'up' exists because resetToLanding() (run before every row's own setup/steps) clicks RESET_CLICK_NAMES by raw xdotool coordinate, not the DOM channel, and cannot recover a target scrolled to a negative on-screen y (a tall form's own 'Back'/'Cancel' pushed off the top by content added below it, e.g. a create-character outcome panel) -- a row that leaves the page scrolled down should scroll back up as its own last step so the NEXT row's resetToLanding can find a landing-reachable control; see create-character-fill-and-submit's own trailing scroll step. Generated docs/testing/ui-smoke-inventory.md is rendered FROM this file by render-inventory.mjs -- edit this file, not the doc. Names in `target`/`selectsNonEmpty` are matched against the live uiProbe.ts snapshot's targets/selects by exact `name` (trimmed textContent || aria-label || placeholder || title || id, and select#<n> for the handful of anonymous <select>s -- see uiProbe.ts). `expect`/`marker`/`forbid` strings are matched against bodyText, which is captured via `innerText` (respects CSS, e.g. `text-transform: uppercase` renders the text differently than its mixed-case source prop/string) -- assert the case that actually renders, not the source string. Global forbid strings (applied by run.mjs to every row unless listed in that row's own `allowGlobalForbid`): 'could be read from the corpus', 'failure', 'Failed to load', 'requires the desktop runtime', 'undefined', 'NaN', '[object Object]', and 'Loading' still present after the row's wait budget.

ItemPickerModal (role=dialog, h2 title = the kind's own title, here 'Add Armor'; portals to document.body, see uiProbe.ts) opened via the Gear tab's Add Armor button (dispatch table in CharacterSheet.tsx also backs Add Gear/Add Spell/Add Feat through the same modal), then closed with Escape. CORRECTED 2026-09-18 (was misdiagnosed as an app defect specific to this catalog -- see git history for the retracted version of this note): `buildItemPickerConfig` routes Add Weapon and Add Armor through the IDENTICAL `loadEquipment('ArmsArmor')` query and the same catalog-agnostic `ItemPickerModal`/`mapEquipmentCatalogEntries` (a plain, uncomputed `.map()`, nothing prerequisite-checked or O(n^2) in it) -- there is no armor-specific render path for anything to be slow in, so a defect that only ever reproduced on 'this specific catalog' was never actually isolated to armor at all, only to whichever row happened to run into the stall. Reproduced directly (2026-09-18): a lone `key: Escape` command genuinely un-acknowledged for 24+ seconds after Add Armor opened, then a fresh command sent moments later (against the same still-open modal) completed in ~100ms -- the same screen-independent webview stall `run.mjs`'s own `CLICK_TARGET_WAIT_MS` comment already documents at length ('anywhere from well under a second up to 60+ seconds ... with no observed correlation to system load', separately confirmed live on settings-tab-* and equipment-catalog-open-and-search, both with zero large payloads). The real bug was harness-side: `pressKey`/`typeText` sent a single command with a bare 5000ms timeout and threw immediately on a miss, while `clickByNameChannel`/`selectByName` already retried the same class of command for up to `CLICK_TARGET_WAIT_MS` (150s) -- an inconsistency between ops, not a per-screen difference. Whichever op happened to be in flight when a stall hit failed fast here (and, via the dialog it left open behind it, blocked every row after it in a sequential run -- confirmed live: sheet-action-level-up-dialog, sheet-action-skill-allocation-dialog and sheet-action-hp-adjust all cascaded BLOCKED immediately after this row's own failure in one continuous run) while an identical stall hitting a `click` step was silently ridden out. Fixed by giving `pressKey`/`typeText` the same retry budget `click`/`select` already had; row confirmed green live 2026-09-18 on a fresh launch immediately after (full run ~2m45s -- the underlying stall still happened, the harness just rode it out instead of failing fast). One more artifact seen mid-investigation, worth naming so a future reader doesn't rediscover it as a new mystery: after one of these stalls, the modal's own DOM/probe state closed correctly (`dialogs: []`, correct screen content in `bodyText`) but the LAST PAINTED FRAME stayed a solid black rectangle over the modal's former screen region indefinitely -- clicks/scrolls landed correctly against the real (invisible) content underneath, only the pixels were stale. Did not clear via further input; cleared by `driver.sh launch` (a fresh WebKitGTK process). Consistent with a software-rasterizer (no GPU under Xvfb, see SKILL.md's own DRI3 note) compositor invalidation bug in this harness's specific renderer path, not a React/app-state bug -- the DOM was already correct the whole time it was showing black.
